items.passage:
As it was, the void turned out to be somewhat like that of a stone-built chimney with here and there a point left projecting. It was so narrow, moreover, that they were able to use both hands and knees in the descent, and by this means they accomplished it.

They went but slowly, and took care to proceed with caution. They knew that a false step, the slipping of a foot or finger, or the breaking of a fragment that gave hold to their hands, would precipitate them to an unknown depth.

They did not go farther than was necessary for quick concealment.
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word "precipitate" most nearly mean?
options: Hurl
Hasten
Condense
Provoke
items.explanation: 지문은 미끄러지거나 손잡이가 부서지면 '알 수 없는 깊이로' 떨어진다는 위험을 말한다. 앞 문장에서 그들이 천천히 조심스럽게 내려갔다는 점도 추락의 위험을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 precipitate는 '내던지다, 떨어뜨리다'의 뜻인 A가 맞다. B는 '서두르게 하다', C는 화학적 '응결시키다', D는 '촉발하다'의 뜻으로 깊이로 떨어진다는 문맥과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: What do modern critics mean by the "healthy completeness" of ancient life, which they are so fond of contrasting with the "heated," "discontented," or imperfect and one-sided existence of modern communities? Is this a mere set of phrases, suited to some imaginary want of the literary critic, but answering to nothing real? Are they to be summarily disposed of as resting upon some tacit assumption of that old-grannyism which delights in asseverating that times are not what they used to be? Is the contrast an imaginary one, due to the softened, cheerful light with which we are wont to contemplate classic antiquity through the charmed medium of its incomparable literature? Or is it a real contrast, worthy of the attention and analysis of the historical inquirer? The answer to these queries will lead us far into the discussion of the subject which we have propounded, and we shall best reach it by considering some aspects of the social condition of ancient Greece.
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word "summarily" most nearly mean?
options: Thoroughly
Dismissively
Gradually
Accurately
items.explanation: 필자는 비평가들의 표현이 '실체 없는 문구'에 불과한지, '옛날이 좋았다'는 가정에 기댄 것으로 치부될 수 있는지를 묻는다. 'disposed of'와 함께 쓰인 summarily는 깊이 따지지 않고 간단히 처리해 버린다는 뜻이다. 따라서 B가 맞다. A는 오히려 반대 의미이고, C와 D는 일축한다는 문맥과 어울리지 않는다.

items.passage: Our own skins are full of holes, or pores, as you know, to let out the extra water and other waste materials in what we call perspiration. The plants need such an arrangement as much as we do. So in their skin we find pores. You see the plant needs a great deal of water. The water is used in making the substance of the plant. It is also used in the sap to carry food about from place to place. Sap contains a great deal of water in order that it may flow easily.
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word "arrangement" most nearly mean?
options: Agreement
Decoration
Structure
Schedule
items.explanation: 앞 문장은 피부에 땀과 노폐물을 내보내는 구멍(pores)이 있다고 설명한다. 이어 식물에도 그런 arrangement가 필요하며 실제로 식물의 표면에 구멍이 있다고 말한다. 따라서 arrangement는 신체의 '구조, 장치'를 뜻하는 C가 맞다. A의 합의, B의 장식, D의 일정은 구멍이라는 신체 구조와 관련이 없다.

items.passage: During this miserable period of suspense and embarrassment, occasioned and prolonged beyond all reason or necessity by the want of lookout ships, the connecting and illuminating thread is the purpose of Nelson, at once clear and firm, to find the French fleet and to fight it the instant found. No other consideration draws his mind aside, except so far as it may facilitate the attainment and fulfilment of this one object. In this one light he sees all things. At the start he writes to St. Vincent: "You may be assured I will fight them the moment I can reach, be they at anchor or under sail."
items.question: As used in the text, what does the word "want" most nearly mean?
options: Desire
Demand
Poverty
Absence
items.explanation: 지문은 불안한 대기 상태가 'lookout ships의 want' 때문에 생기고 길어졌다고 말한다. 정찰선이 있었다면 프랑스 함대를 빨리 찾았을 것이므로, 여기서 want는 '부족, 없음'을 뜻한다. 따라서 D가 맞다. A의 욕망, B의 요구는 의미가 다르고, C의 빈곤은 사람의 형편에 쓰는 말이라 정찰선이 없다는 상황과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: With a quick shake of the head, as if doing violence to himself, he turned his face westward and pushed through the Low Countries to the sea. There he was met by his English peers, by Longchamp, by his brother of Rouen, by men who loved and men who feared; but he had no word for any. Grim and hungry he stalked through the lane they made him, on to the galley; folded in his cloak there, lonely he paced the bridge. He was rowed to the west with his eyes fixed always on the east, away from his kingdom to where he supposed his longing to be.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift that occurs in the text?
options: It moves from a joyful reunion with his peers to a quiet farewell to his brother.
It moves from a calm voyage at sea to an anxious march through the Low Countries.
It moves from a brief act of forced resolve to a portrait of his lonely longing.
It moves from open fear of his enemies to a growing trust in those who love him.
items.explanation: 첫 문장에서 그는 '스스로에게 폭력을 가하듯' 고개를 저으며 서쪽으로 향하는 결단을 내린다. 그러나 이후에는 누구에게도 말을 건네지 않고 홀로 갑판을 거닐며 눈은 계속 동쪽을 향하는 외로운 그리움이 그려진다. 따라서 C가 맞다. A는 기쁜 재회가 없으므로, B는 순서가 반대이므로, D는 신뢰가 커지는 내용이 없으므로 틀리다.

items.passage:
Gone forever “out from the golden day.” Just the release he had dreamed of, perhaps wished for, yet hardly prayed for. Men seldom do that; only women drop down on their knees and pour out their hearts that way, rising sometimes to say it is all for the best.

Emory at last rose from his chair and left his room. It was almost midnight, and the streets were deserted when he reached the City Park. A few steps brought him to a seat under a tree, near which a fountain splashed, a place where he had often sat alone.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift that occurs in the text?
options: It moves from a cheerful memory of the past to a bitter complaint about the city.
It moves from a description of women praying to an account of Emory's own prayer.
It moves from a lively scene in the park to a quiet return to Emory's room.
It moves from reflection on a release to a quiet account of Emory's late walk.
items.explanation: 첫 단락은 꿈꾸던 해방이 찾아왔다는 생각과 남녀가 슬픔에 반응하는 방식에 대한 성찰이다. 둘째 단락은 Emory가 마침내 일어나 자정 무렵 텅 빈 거리를 지나 공원 벤치에 앉는 행동을 담담히 서술한다. 따라서 D가 맞다. A는 도시에 대한 불평이 없고, B는 Emory가 기도하지 않으며, C는 이동 순서가 반대이다.

items.passage: The traditions of the old system are, however, unquestionably a better basis for good hotel-keeping than anything we have at the North. The first condition of excellence in all places of entertainment for man and beast is exactingness on the part of the public. To be well cared for you must expect it and be used to it, and this condition the Southerners fulfil in a much higher degree than we do. They look for more attention, and they therefore get it; and the waiter world, partly from habit and partly, no doubt, from race temperament, render it with a cheerfulness we are not familiar with here. But the superiority of manners in all classes is very striking.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift that occurs in the text?
options: It moves from praising Southern hotel service to noting Southern manners broadly.
It moves from criticizing Southern hotels to defending Northern hotel customs.
It moves from describing Northern waiters to complaining about Southern guests.
It moves from doubting the old system to rejecting the idea of good manners.
items.explanation: 필자는 먼저 남부 사람들이 서비스를 기대하기 때문에 호텔의 응대가 더 낫다고 설명한다. 마지막에 'But'으로 전환하며 모든 계층에 걸친 남부의 예절 자체가 뛰어나다고 범위를 넓힌다. 따라서 A가 맞다. B와 C는 남부를 비판하는 내용이 없으므로, D는 예절을 거부하지 않으므로 틀리다.

items.passage:
The botanical productions of the hills seemed also to undergo a considerable change, indicating, as we would fain hope, that a better country is not far off. Several new plants were acquired today, some of which were very beautiful. Our course made good was N. 71. E., distance thirteen miles and a half.

August 7.--The horses suffered much from want of food and water; but it is absolutely necessary to proceed and get into a better country with all the expedition which we are capable of using, and which the nature of this country will allow. It is some consolation to us that the horses are but lightly loaded, by reason of our not being now encumbered with much provisions, and are consequently enabled to travel farther and better.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift that occurs in the text?
options: It moves from fear of hostile people to relief at finding fresh provisions.
It moves from hopeful notes on new plants to concern about the suffering horses.
It moves from complaints about heavy loads to praise for the fertile country.
It moves from distress over lost horses to joy at reaching their destination.
items.explanation: 첫 단락은 식물의 변화가 '더 나은 땅이 멀지 않다'는 희망을 준다고 기록하며 새 식물을 모았다고 적는다. 8월 7일 기록에서는 말들이 먹이와 물 부족으로 고생한다는 걱정으로 바뀐다. 따라서 B가 맞다. A는 적대적인 사람이 없고, C는 짐이 가볍다고 했으며, D는 목적지에 도착하지 않았으므로 틀리다.

items.passage:
To be the worst dressed would call for courage--of just the sort she prided herself on having. Also, it would look original, would cause talk--would give her the coveted sense of achievement.

When she descended to show herself to her father and say good night to him, she was certainly dressed by the same pattern that caused him to be talked about throughout that region. Her gown was mussed, had been mended obviously in several places, had not been in its best day becoming. But this was not all.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: A woman's dress is praised by her father, and then she decides to change it.
A father criticizes his daughter, and then she explains her reasons to him.
A woman reasons about dressing badly, and then her shabby gown is described.
A gown is mended in several places, and then a woman refuses to wear it.
items.explanation: 첫 단락은 가장 못 입는 것이 용기이자 독창성이 되어 화제가 될 것이라는 그녀의 생각을 보여 준다. 둘째 단락은 그녀가 실제로 구겨지고 여러 번 기운 옷을 입고 아버지 앞에 내려오는 모습을 묘사한다. 따라서 C가 맞다. A와 B는 아버지의 반응이 나오지 않으므로, D는 그녀가 옷을 실제로 입었으므로 틀리다.

items.passage:
Auzeem concealed the lamp under his cloak, and prayed his companions, in a low voice, to remain as they were for a few moments. The knocking still continued. It was evidently at the outer door of their late prison. Orders were issued repeatedly to open the door, and threats were uttered to force it, if these orders were not instantly obeyed. A loud crash followed soon after, and a crowd of persons were heard rushing into the apartments.

Kazim could not help feeling strange suspicions passing through his mind, while this scene was going on. Auzeem had by no means as yet won his entire confidence. The acts of that minister, during the two years of the usurpation which had just elapsed, were all in favour of the success of the Persian.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: A minister explains a plan, and then Kazim agrees to follow it without question.
Kazim hears knocking, and then he flees the prison alone to warn the Persian.
Guards break into a room, and then Auzeem is arrested in front of his friends.
Noises of a break-in are described, and then Kazim's doubts about Auzeem appear.
items.explanation: 첫 단락은 Auzeem이 등불을 숨기는 동안 문을 두드리고 부수며 사람들이 몰려 들어오는 소리를 묘사한다. 둘째 단락은 Kazim이 Auzeem을 완전히 믿지 못하고 의심을 품는 내면으로 초점이 옮겨 간다. 따라서 D가 맞다. A는 Kazim이 의심하므로, B는 혼자 도망가지 않으므로, C는 체포 장면이 없으므로 틀리다.

items.passage: In a moment more its beautiful black, scarlet-bordered and white-spotted wings are seen fluttering among the leaves, alighting now here, now there, each brief visit leaving a visible witness if we care to look for it. It has now settled upon a leaf within easy reach. Creeping along its edge, it is soon hanging beneath, but only for a second, and is off again on the wing. Let us pluck the leaf. Upon looking beneath it we may see the pretty token of the Red Admiral, a tiny egg which we may well preserve for our microscope.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: A butterfly's movements are traced, and then the egg it leaves is revealed.
A butterfly's egg is examined, and then the insect's wings are described.
A collector catches a butterfly, and then explains how to preserve its wings.
A leaf is studied closely, and then a butterfly is seen landing far away.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 Red Admiral 나비가 잎 사이를 날아다니다가 잎에 앉고 매달렸다 날아가는 움직임을 따라간다. 이어 그 잎을 따서 뒤를 보면 나비가 남긴 작은 알을 발견하게 된다고 말한다. 따라서 A가 맞다. B는 순서가 반대이고, C는 나비를 잡지 않으며, D는 나비가 가까운 잎에 앉으므로 틀리다.

items.passage: Not being familiar with the channel I am going it blind, and I don’t want to knock a hole in her, or run her high and dry on a sand-bar before I know it. I think it would be safest to stay here for a while, and let our pursuers get ahead of us, so that we will be in their wake instead of having them in ours. Perhaps you had better talk it up among the boys and see what they think of it. While you are about it, find out if there is any one in the band who knows the river.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the sentence "I think it would be safest to stay here for a while, and let our pursuers get ahead of us" in the text as a whole?
options: It recalls a past mistake that the speaker made while sailing the river.
It states the speaker's proposed plan in response to the risks he describes.
It rejects a plan that the boys in the band have already agreed upon.
It reveals that the speaker knows the river channel better than anyone.
items.explanation: 화자는 먼저 물길을 몰라 배에 구멍을 내거나 모래톱에 걸릴까 걱정한다고 말한다. 해당 문장은 그 위험에 대한 대응으로 잠시 머물며 추격자들을 앞서 보내자는 계획을 제시한다. 이후 이 계획을 일행과 상의하라고 부탁하므로 B가 맞다. A는 과거의 실수가 아니고, C는 일행이 아직 동의하지 않았으며, D는 화자가 물길을 모른다고 했으므로 틀리다.

items.passage:
The dull glitter, all-pervading, lighted up her forest “sanctuary”; not a sound was heard, except when, once, a snapped twig came rustling to the ground.

Her husband had doubted her honor. Even supposing he had done so for the moment only, during the briefest flash of thought. What did that matter? He had doubted her. Other words and acts now came falling into their places, deepening an impression never before perceived. She brushed them away indignantly; she wanted none of these. It was enough.

She could never go back to him. How could she see him? How speak to him? How could daily contact be possible between a husband and the wife whom, for one instant only, his thought had sullied?
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the sentence "Her husband had doubted her honor." in the text as a whole?
options: It describes the quiet forest where the woman has come to rest.
It explains why the woman's husband has begun to search for her.
It names the hurt that drives the woman's resolve not to return.
It suggests that the woman has forgiven her husband's brief doubt.
items.explanation: 첫 단락은 고요한 숲의 '성소'를 묘사하고, 해당 문장은 남편이 그녀의 정조를 의심했다는 상처를 처음 밝힌다. 이어 그녀는 그 의심이 한순간이었더라도 상관없다고 생각하고 마지막 단락에서 다시는 돌아갈 수 없다고 결심한다. 따라서 C가 맞다. A는 숲 묘사는 앞 문장의 역할이고, B는 남편의 수색이 없으며, D는 용서하지 않으므로 틀리다.

items.passage:
Even the unity of the species is far from settled, science still debates whether there is one race of men or whether there are more than a hundred. Man acts on man no doubt, but he also acts on other animals, and other animals on him. Wherein does the special unity or the special bond consist? Above all what constitutes the holiness? Individual men are not holy, a large proportion of them are very much the reverse. Why is the aggregate holy? Let the unit be a complex phenomenon, an organism or whatever name science may give it, what multiple of it will be a rational object of worship?

For our own part we cannot conceive worship being offered by a sane worshipper to any but a conscious being, in other words to a person.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the sentence "Individual men are not holy, a large proportion of them are very much the reverse." in the text as a whole?
options: It praises the moral goodness of most individual human beings.
It summarizes a scientific finding about the unity of the species.
It offers the writer's final conclusion about whom people may worship.
It supports the writer's doubt that humanity as a whole is holy.
items.explanation: 필자는 인류 전체를 숭배 대상으로 삼는 생각에 의문을 제기하며 연속된 질문을 던진다. 해당 문장은 개인들이 거룩하지 않고 오히려 그 반대라는 근거를 제시해, 바로 뒤의 '왜 총합은 거룩한가'라는 의문을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 D가 맞다. A는 반대 의미이고, B는 과학적 발견이 아니며, C의 결론은 마지막 단락에 따로 나온다.

items.passage: If I were--if I were, I would give up my ship. I would give up everything, to follow you. I can’t explain; that is part of the hardness of it. I only want you to know it,--that if certain things were different, if everything was different, I might tell you that I believe I should have a right to speak to you. Perhaps some day it will change; but probably then it will be too late. Meanwhile, I have no right of any kind. I don’t want to trouble you, and I don’t ask of you--anything! It is only to have spoken just once. I don’t make you understand, of course.
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward the person he addresses?
options: He is angry that she has refused to listen to him.
He is amused by the confusion his words have caused.
He is devoted to her but feels he has no right to speak.
He is indifferent to her and eager to return to his ship.
items.explanation: 화자는 사정만 달랐다면 배를 포함한 모든 것을 버리고 그녀를 따르겠다고 말한다. 그러나 지금은 자신에게 '어떤 권리도 없다'며 아무것도 요구하지 않는다고 덧붙인다. 따라서 깊은 애정과 함께 말할 자격이 없다는 체념이 담긴 C가 맞다. A의 분노, B의 재미, D의 무관심은 지문의 간절한 어조와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: The subject of this sketch reached the ripe old age of eleven with all functions and faculties unimpaired, save sight, which, we are compelled to record, was totally obscured. I happened to be with him when he came to the painful realization of his great misfortune. It was during his accustomed late-in-the-afternoon walk. Failing to find his way along the sidewalk he had stopped, while I, without seeing him, had passed on, but only for a short distance, when I was attracted by a most pitiful and grief-stricken cry.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the subject of the sketch?
options: Mocking amusement at the subject's clumsy walk
Cool detachment from the subject's daily habits
Mild annoyance at being delayed on the sidewalk
Sympathetic concern for the subject's misfortune
items.explanation: 서술자는 주인공이 시력을 잃은 것을 '기록하지 않을 수 없다'며 안타깝게 전하고 그것을 '큰 불행'이라 부른다. 또 주인공의 '가장 애처롭고 비통한 울음'에 이끌려 돌아본다고 서술한다. 따라서 공감 어린 염려를 나타낸 D가 맞다. A의 조롱, B의 냉담, C의 짜증은 이런 표현과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
There is not in the wide world so tempting a sweet
As that trifle where custard and macaroons meet.
Oh! the latest sweet tooth from my head must depart
Ere the taste of that trifle shall not win my heart.

Yet it is not the sugar that's thrown in between,
Nor the peel of the lemon so candied and green,
'T is not the rich cream that's whipped up by a mill,
Oh, no; it is something more exquisite still!
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward the trifle?
options: Playful adoration
Polite indifference
Mild disappointment
Cautious suspicion
items.explanation: 화자는 세상에 이 trifle만큼 유혹적인 단것이 없다고 말한다. 또 마지막 단것 이빨이 빠질 때까지 그 맛이 마음을 사로잡을 것이라고 과장하며, 재료보다 더 '절묘한' 무언가가 있다고 노래한다. 따라서 장난스러운 애정을 뜻하는 A가 맞다. B의 무관심, C의 실망, D의 의심은 찬미하는 어조와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: A little self-denial would have saved them, and those depending on them, from many sorrows. A saving habit is good. "It is coarse thinking to confound spending with generosity, or saving with meanness." The man who puts by a little week by week or year by year, against possible contingencies is wise. However small may be our salary and limited our income, we should try and save part of it. Every young man should be a member of a savings bank, or a benefit club, by means of which he can make provision for the future.
items.question: Which choice best describes the writer's attitude toward saving money?
options: Doubtful that small incomes can ever be saved
Firmly convinced that saving is wise and needed
Worried that saving often turns people mean
Amused by young men who join savings banks
items.explanation: 필자는 저축 습관이 좋으며 조금씩 모으는 사람이 '현명하다'고 말한다. 또 수입이 적어도 일부를 저축해야 하고 모든 청년이 저축은행에 가입해야 한다고 권한다. 따라서 저축을 확신 있게 지지하는 B가 맞다. A는 적은 수입으로도 저축하라고 했고, C는 인용문이 저축을 인색함과 혼동하지 말라고 했으며, D의 재미는 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
We heard there good accounts of the improved and improving literary taste of the place, shown in the increasing number of book societies, and the superior character of the works supplied to their orders. Mr. Flash and his partner are in favour of the protection of foreign literary property, as a matter of interest as well as principle.

We next went to the painting-room of a young artist, Mr. Beard, whose works pleased me more than those of any other American artist. When I heard his story, and saw what he had already achieved, I could not doubt that, if he lived, he would run a noble career. The chief doubt was about his health, the doubt which hangs over the destiny of almost every individual of eminent promise in America.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Mr. Beard?
options: She dismisses his paintings as weaker than other work.
She envies the success he has gained in the city.
She admires his talent but worries about his health.
She doubts that his story of his career is true.
items.explanation: 서술자는 Beard의 작품이 다른 어떤 미국 화가의 작품보다 마음에 들었다고 말하며 그가 훌륭한 경력을 쌓을 것을 의심하지 않는다고 한다. 그러나 가장 큰 걱정은 그의 건강이라고 덧붙인다. 따라서 재능에 대한 감탄과 건강에 대한 염려를 함께 담은 C가 맞다. A는 반대이고, B의 질투와 D의 불신은 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: The old gentleman ran against me on the platform, penetrated my disguise at once and asked me where I was going. I told him, and then he remarked that I should do no such thing, and he started me back home in a hurry. When he got there he gave me a lecture, told me that such a proceeding on my part was not honest and would ruin my reputation. In fact, he made me thoroughly ashamed of myself. The team from Clinton had to get along without my services, but I shall never forget what a time I had in getting the dye out of my hair and the stain from my skin.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The narrator describes how proud he felt after playing for the team from Clinton.
The narrator explains how he learned to apply dye and stain as a clever disguise.
The narrator complains that an old gentleman unfairly ruined his reputation.
The narrator recalls how an old gentleman shamed him out of a dishonest plan.
items.explanation: 노신사는 변장한 화자를 알아보고 집으로 돌려보낸 뒤 그런 행동은 정직하지 않다고 훈계한다. 화자는 그 일로 '철저히 부끄러워졌다'고 말하며, 결국 Clinton 팀은 그 없이 경기를 했다. 따라서 D가 맞다. A는 경기에 나가지 않았고, B는 변장 방법 설명이 요지가 아니며, C는 노신사가 오히려 평판을 지켜 주려 했으므로 틀리다.
